chunks: And Ali ibn Mahziyar narrated from Hammad ibn Isa from Husayn ibn Mukhtar from Abu Basir who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) married a woman, and the door was closed. He said, 'Open it, and you shall have what you asked for.' When they opened it, he reconciled with them. Ibn Abi Umayr (may Allah have mercy on him) used to say: 'Indeed, the narrations have differed regarding this matter. Therefore, the way to reconcile between them is that the judge should rule based on the apparent fact and obligate the man the entire dowry if he lowered the curtain, except that the woman is not entitled to take more than half of the dowry in her relationship with Allah. This is a good opinion and does not contradict what we have previously stated, because we only obligated half the dowry when there was knowledge of non-consummation and the ability to know that. But when the knowledge and the ability to know are removed, the statement is what Ibn Abi Umayr said. And that which confirms what we mentioned is also what he narrated:'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on the full or half dowry when it is uncertain whether marital consummation occurred?
ai.summary: This narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* highlights the jurisprudential debate regarding the full versus half dowry when consummation status is ambiguous, specifically citing the view of Ibn Abi Umayr. It resolves conflicting reports by distinguishing between clear knowledge of non-consummation and situations of uncertainty where the judge rules based on the apparent fact (lowering the curtain). This approach ensures the husband bears the full financial obligation while the woman retains spiritual discretion over her share.
